items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: And Jimmy was so surprised, he turned around and shook my hand!

ctx.x: that's all Sidney wanted to hear. And they just battled backward and forward, backward and forward, backward and forward. That was a great night in the Saratoga Club, because all the musicians were around and just the two of them, backwards and forwards.

It did me good because I didn't have to play it! Because Jimmy Dorsey was sitting up on the bandstand, you know, and I had just gotten up. Jimmy and I had just... Because at that time, Jimmy had recorded a number, a saxophone solo on a number "Sensation," and I knew the number -- I knew the solo, you know. And we was on the stand playing "Sensation," and just before Jimmy's solo, I played -- and I played his solo on the number. Which was very unprofessional, you know. And Jimmy was so surprised, he turned around…

Well, we had a good time, though. But right after that, then Bechet was introduced, and that's when him and Benny Goodman got to battlin' up there. But it was all in fun. Nobody got killed or anything in that battle.
